record.paper_title: The origin and evolution of transition discs: successes, problems and open questions
record.original_question: For the low-mm-flux, small-hole transition-disc population that is probably undergoing true disc dispersal, what are the actual gas and dust structures inside the inferred cavities: do the spectral-energy-distribution-inferred holes exist when imaged directly, is there any non-axisymmetric structure, and how much gas remains inside those cavities?

evidence.quote: In most cases all the information in hole size and dust distribution come from photometry and SED fitting.
Additionally, given the hole sizes are small and mm fluxes are low, no imaging campaign has confirmed the presence of the holes inferred from the SED or probed any non-axisymmteric structure.
Since these discs are likely to actually be discs in transition, more observations are required to constrain the structures in both gas and dust of these discs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the population of protoplanetary transition discs characterized by (i) low millimetre continuum fluxes and (ii) small inner cavities ("holes") whose existence has been inferred indirectly by fitting parametric models to the unresolved spectral energy distribution (SED), rather than from spatially resolved imaging. Such objects are widely conjectured to represent discs that are genuinely undergoing dispersal of their primordial gas-and-dust content (as opposed to discs hosting massive embedded planets or large dust traps). Determine, by means of high-resolution direct imaging in dust continuum and gas tracers (e.g. resolved sub-millimetre/millimetre interferometric observations and resolved molecular-line observations) the following for this specific subpopulation:

(a) Whether the inner dust cavities inferred from SED modelling are confirmed when the discs are imaged at resolutions sufficient to resolve the predicted hole radius; that is, quantify the dust surface density profile Σ_dust(r) inside the SED-inferred hole radius R_hole and decide whether Σ_dust(r) is consistent with a true depleted cavity or with a continuous, unbroken distribution.

(b) Whether any non-axisymmetric structure (e.g. azimuthal asymmetries, lopsided dust concentrations, spiral features) is present in the dust or gas distribution within or near the cavity, and characterise its amplitude and morphology.

(c) The amount of gas remaining inside the cavities, expressed as a gas surface density profile Σ_gas(r) for r < R_hole and an integrated gas mass M_gas(r < R_hole), together with the gas-to-dust ratio in the cavity region.

Provide quantitative constraints (or upper limits) on Σ_dust(r), Σ_gas(r), the gas-to-dust ratio, and any asymmetry contrast for this low-mm-flux, small-hole subclass of transition discs.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is an observational/astrophysical open problem about confirming SED-inferred cavities, asymmetries, and residual gas content in low-millimetre-flux, small-hole transition discs. While ALMA has resolved many bright, large-cavity transition discs in the years since the question was posed, the specific low-flux, small-hole subpopulation remains observationally challenging and has not been comprehensively characterised in dust morphology, asymmetry, and interior gas content. The problem therefore appears to remain open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: The origin and evolution of transition discs
status_evidence.snippet: Notes that hole sizes are small and mm fluxes are low, and no imaging campaign has confirmed the SED-inferred holes or probed non-axisymmetric structure for this subpopulation.
status_evidence.claim: At the time of posing, no resolved imaging existed for this subpopulation; this remains a recognised observational gap.
